statements.subject: message
statements.description: A new DHCP message type, DHCPINFORM, has been added; see section 3.4, 4.3 and 4.4 for details.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client IP address; only filled in if client is in BOUND, RENEW or REBINDING state and can respond to ARP requests.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client IP address; only filled in if client is in BOUND, RENEW or REBINDING state and can respond to ARP requests.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client IP address; only filled in if client is in BOUND, RENEW or REBINDING state and can respond to ARP requests.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client IP address; only filled in if client is in BOUND, RENEW or REBINDING state and can respond to ARP requests.
statements.guard_semantics: protocol.state = BOUND | protocol.state = RENEW | protocol.state = REBINDING

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may extend its lease with subsequent requests.
statements.trigger: client sends subsequent lease extension request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may issue a message to release the address back to the server when the client no longer needs the address.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The allocation mechanism will reuse addresses whose lease has expired.
actions: mark expired-lease address as available for reuse

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The allocating server SHOULD probe the reused address before allocating the address, e.g., with an ICMP echo request.
actions: probe reused address (e.g., ICMP echo request)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD probe the newly received address, e.g., with ARP.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The period over which a network address is allocated to a client is referred to as a 'lease'. The allocation mechanism guarantees not to reallocate that address within the requested time.
statements.guard_semantics: address remains allocated to client for duration of lease; server must not reallocate before lease.expired = true

statements.subject: message
statements.description: One particular option - the 'DHCP message type' option - must be included in every DHCP message. This option defines the 'type' of the DHCP message.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The 'op' field of each DHCP message sent from a client to a server contains BOOTREQUEST.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: BOOTREPLY is used in the 'op' field of each DHCP message sent from a server to a client.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Additional options may be allowed, required, or not allowed, depending on the DHCP message type.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: the client reverts to INIT state and restarts the initialization process

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Begins initialization - client begins the DHCP initialization process (figure 3)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Determines configuration - server determines configuration in response to DHCPDISCOVER (figure 3)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Collects replies - client collects DHCPOFFER replies from one or more servers (figure 3)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Selects configuration - client selects one server and configuration from received DHCPOFFER messages (figure 3)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Commits configuration - selected server commits the binding for the client to persistent storage (figure 3)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Initialization complete - client is configured after receiving DHCPACK (figure 3)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Graceful shutdown - client relinquishes its lease by sending DHCPRELEASE (figure 3)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Discards lease - server discards lease after receiving DHCPRELEASE from client (figure 3)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client broadcasts a DHCPDISCOVER message on its local physical subnet to begin initialization

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Each server may respond with a DHCPOFFER message that includes an available network address; server determines configuration

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client receives one or more DHCPOFFER messages from one or more servers. The client may choose to wait for multiple responses. The client chooses one server from which to request configuration parameters.
actions: select server based on offered configuration parameters

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client broadcasts a DHCPREQUEST message that MUST include the 'server identifier' option to indicate which server it has selected
actions: broadcast DHCPREQUEST with server identifier option
set requested IP address to yiaddr from DHCPOFFER

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server selected in the DHCPREQUEST message commits the binding for the client to persistent storage and responds with a DHCPACK message containing the configuration parameters

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client receives the DHCPACK message with configuration parameters. The client SHOULD perform a final check on the parameters (e.g., ARP for allocated network address). At this point, the client is configured.
actions: perform final check on parameters (e.g., ARP)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client detects that the address is already in use (e.g., through the use of ARP), the client MUST send a DHCPDECLINE message to the server and restarts the configuration process. The client SHOULD wait a minimum of ten seconds before restarting.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client receives a DHCPNAK message, the client restarts the configuration process

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client times out and retransmits the DHCPDISCOVER message if the client receives no DHCPOFFER messages

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client times out and retransmits the DHCPREQUEST message if the client receives neither a DHCPACK or a DHCPNAK message
statements.pre_cond: client.state = Selects configuration & received_DHCPACK = false & received_DHCPNAK = false

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client receives neither a DHCPACK or a DHCPNAK message after employing the retransmission algorithm, the client reverts to INIT state and restarts the initialization process. The client SHOULD notify the user that the initialization process has failed and is restarting.
statements.pre_cond: client.state = Selects configuration & retransmission_complete = true & received_DHCPACK = false & received_DHCPNAK = false

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may choose to relinquish its lease on a network address by sending a DHCPRELEASE message to the server

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server discards lease after receiving DHCPRELEASE from client during graceful shutdown (figure 3)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the selected server is unable to satisfy the DHCPREQUEST message (e.g., the requested network address has been allocated), the server SHOULD respond with a DHCPNAK message

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Those servers not selected by the DHCPREQUEST message use the message as notification that the client has declined that server's offer
actions: treat as decline notification for offered address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: This action corresponds to the client moving to the INIT state in the DHCP state diagram, which is described in section 4.4.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: This corresponds to moving to BOUND state in the client state transition diagram shown in figure 5.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Figure 4 shows 'Initialization complete' as the state reached by the client after receiving DHCPACK when reusing a previously allocated network address.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client broadcasts a DHCPREQUEST message on its local subnet including the client's network address in the 'requested IP address' option when reusing a previously allocated network address.
actions: broadcast DHCPREQUEST with requested IP address option set to previously allocated address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client receives the DHCPACK message with configuration parameters. The client performs a final check on the parameters and notes the duration of the lease. At this point, the client is configured.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client detects that the IP address in the DHCPACK message is already in use, the client MUST send a DHCPDECLINE message to the server and restarts the configuration process by requesting a new network address. This action corresponds to the client moving to the INIT state in the DHCP state diagram.
statements.trigger: IP address in DHCPACK detected already in use
actions: restart configuration process requesting new network address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client receives a DHCPNAK message, it cannot reuse its remembered network address. It must instead request a new address by restarting the configuration process. This action also corresponds to the client moving to the INIT state in the DHCP state diagram.
actions: restart configuration process using full procedure

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client times out and retransmits the DHCPREQUEST message if the client receives neither a DHCPACK nor a DHCPNAK message. The client retransmits the DHCPREQUEST according to the retransmission algorithm in section 4.1.
statements.trigger: timeout (no DHCPACK and no DHCPNAK received)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client receives neither a DHCPACK or a DHCPNAK message after employing the retransmission algorithm, the client MAY choose to use the previously allocated network address and configuration parameters for the remainder of the unexpired lease. This corresponds to moving to BOUND state in the client state transition diagram shown in figure 5.
statements.trigger: retransmission algorithm exhausted with no DHCPACK and no DHCPNAK
statements.pre_cond: client.received_dhcpack = false & client.received_dhcpnak = false & client.retransmission_exhausted = true & client.lease_unexpired = true
actions: use previously allocated network address and configuration parameters for remainder of unexpired lease

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client may choose to relinquish its lease on a network address by sending a DHCPRELEASE message to the server. The client identifies the lease to be released with its 'client identifier', or 'chaddr' and network address in the DHCPRELEASE message.
actions: send DHCPRELEASE to server with client identifier or chaddr and network address

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the client's request is invalid (e.g., the client has moved to a new subnet), servers SHOULD respond with a DHCPNAK message to the client.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a client has obtained a network address through some other means (e.g., manual configuration), it may use a DHCPINFORM request message to obtain other local configuration parameters.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers receiving a DHCPINFORM message construct a DHCPACK message with any local configuration parameters appropriate for the client without: allocating a new address, checking for an existing binding, filling in 'yiaddr' or including lease time parameters.
actions: construct DHCPACK with local configuration parameters

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The servers SHOULD unicast the DHCPACK reply to the address given in the 'ciaddr' field of the DHCPINFORM message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD check the network address in a DHCPINFORM message for consistency, but MUST NOT check for an existing lease. The server forms a DHCPACK message containing the configuration parameters for the requesting client and sends the DHCPACK message directly to the client.
actions: check network address in DHCPINFORM for consistency
do not check for existing lease

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Servers receiving a DHCPINFORM message construct a DHCPACK message without filling in 'yiaddr' or including lease time parameters.
statements.guard_semantics: DHCPACK is sent in response to DHCPINFORM

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Servers receiving a DHCPINFORM message construct a DHCPACK message without including lease time parameters.
statements.guard_semantics: DHCPACK is sent in response to DHCPINFORM

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client fills in the 'ciaddr' field only when correctly configured with an IP address in BOUND, RENEWING or REBINDING state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client fills in the 'ciaddr' field only when correctly configured with an IP address in BOUND, RENEWING or REBINDING state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client fills in the 'ciaddr' field only when correctly configured with an IP address in BOUND, RENEWING or REBINDING state.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The client fills in the 'ciaddr' field only when correctly configured with an IP address in BOUND, RENEWING or REBINDING state.
statements.guard_semantics: protocol.state = BOUND | protocol.state = RENEWING | protocol.state = REBINDING

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the client includes a list of parameters in a DHCPDISCOVER message, it MUST include that list in any subsequent DHCPREQUEST messages.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a server receives a DHCPREQUEST message with an invalid 'requested IP address', the server SHOULD respond to the client with a DHCPNAK message and may choose to report the problem to the system administrator.
statements.trigger: receive DHCPREQUEST with invalid requested IP address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client SHOULD use DHCP to reacquire or verify its IP address and network parameters whenever the local network parameters may have changed; e.g., at system boot time or after a disconnection from the local network.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a client has knowledge of a previous network address and is unable to contact a local DHCP server, the client may continue to use the previous network address until the lease for that address expires.
statements.pre_cond: client.previous_network_address != null & client.dhcp_server_reachable = false & client.lease_expired = false

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the lease expires before the client can contact a DHCP server, the client must immediately discontinue use of the previous network address and may inform local users of the problem.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCP clients are responsible for all message retransmission. The client MUST adopt a retransmission strategy that incorporates a randomized exponential backoff algorithm to determine the delay between retransmissions. The retransmission delay SHOULD be doubled with subsequent retransmissions up to a maximum of 64 seconds.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client that cannot receive unicast IP datagrams until its protocol software has been configured with an IP address SHOULD set the BROADCAST bit in the 'flags' field to 1 in any DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST messages that client sends. A client that can receive unicast IP datagrams before its protocol software has been configured SHOULD clear the BROADCAST bit to 0.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the 'giaddr' field in a DHCP message from a client is non-zero, the server sends any return messages to the 'DHCP server' port on the BOOTP relay agent whose address appears in 'giaddr'. If the 'giaddr' field is zero and the 'ciaddr' field is nonzero, then the server unicasts DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK messages to the address in 'ciaddr'. If 'giaddr' is zero and 'ciaddr' is zero, and the broadcast bit is set, then the server broadcasts DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK messages to 0xffffffff. If the broadcast bit is not set and 'giaddr' is zero and 'ciaddr' is zero, then the server unicasts DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK messages to the client's hardware address and 'yiaddr' address. In all cases, when 'giaddr' is zero, the server broadcasts any DHCPNAK messages to 0xffffffff.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCP clients MUST use the IP address provided in the 'server identifier' option for any unicast requests to the DHCP server.
statements.guard_semantics: destination address for client unicast requests to server

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The 'xid' field is used by the client to match incoming DHCP messages with pending requests. A DHCP client MUST choose 'xid's in such a way as to minimize the chance of using an 'xid' identical to one used by another client.
statements.guard_semantics: matches incoming DHCP messages with pending client requests

statements.subject: server
statements.description: DHCP servers are not required to respond to every DHCPDISCOVER and DHCPREQUEST message they receive.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY choose to explicitly provide the identifier through the 'client identifier' option.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client supplies a 'client identifier', the client MUST use the same 'client identifier' in all subsequent messages.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST use that identifier to identify the client. If the client does not provide a 'client identifier' option, the server MUST use the contents of the 'chaddr' field to identify the client.
statements.guard_semantics: message.client_identifier_present = true -> use client_identifier; message.client_identifier_present = false -> use chaddr

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCP clients are free to use any strategy in selecting a DHCP server among those from which the client receives a DHCPOFFER message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A DHCP server processes incoming DHCP messages from a client based on the current state of the binding for that client.
statements.guard_semantics: Server selects processing logic based on binding.state for the originating client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A DHCP server can receive DHCPDISCOVER from a client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A DHCP server can receive DHCPREQUEST from a client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A DHCP server can receive DHCPDECLINE from a client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A DHCP server can receive DHCPRELEASE from a client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A DHCP server can receive DHCPINFORM from a client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When a server receives a DHCPDISCOVER message from a client, the server chooses a network address for the requesting client. Once the network address and lease have been determined, the server constructs a DHCPOFFER message with the offered configuration parameters and sends the DHCPOFFER message to the requesting client.
actions: insert xid from DHCPDISCOVER into DHCPOFFER xid field

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If no address is available, the server may choose to report the problem to the system administrator.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY, for administrative reasons, assign an address other than the one requested, or may refuse to allocate an address to a particular client even though free addresses are available.
actions: refuse to allocate address to client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD NOT reuse the selected network address before the client responds to the server's DHCPOFFER message. The server may choose to record the address as offered to the client.
actions: record address as offered to client
do not reuse selected network address until client responds

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during SELECTING state: Client inserts the address of the selected server in 'server identifier'.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during INIT-REBOOT state: The client is seeking to verify a previously allocated, cached configuration.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during RENEWING state: the client is completely configured, and is trying to extend its lease. This message will be unicast.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during REBINDING state: the client is completely configured, and is trying to extend its lease. This message MUST be broadcast to the 0xffffffff IP broadcast address.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during SELECTING state: Client inserts the address of the selected server in 'server identifier', 'ciaddr' MUST be zero, 'requested IP address' MUST be filled in with the yiaddr value from the chosen DHCPOFFER.
actions: set server_identifier to selected server address
set requested_ip_address to yiaddr from chosen DHCPOFFER

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client receives no acceptable offers, the client may choose to try another DHCPDISCOVER message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during INIT-REBOOT state: 'server identifier' MUST NOT be filled in, 'requested IP address' option MUST be filled in with client's notion of its previously assigned address. 'ciaddr' MUST be zero.
actions: set requested_ip_address to previously assigned address

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server SHOULD send a DHCPNAK message to the client if the 'requested IP address' is incorrect, or is on the wrong network.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the DHCP server has no record of this client, then it MUST remain silent, and MAY output a warning to the network administrator.
actions: may output warning to network administrator

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during RENEWING state: 'server identifier' MUST NOT be filled in, 'requested IP address' option MUST NOT be filled in, 'ciaddr' MUST be filled in with client's IP address. This message will be unicast.
statements.post_cond: message.server_identifier = null & message.requested_ip_address = null & message.ciaddr = client.ip_address
actions: set ciaddr to client IP address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST generated during REBINDING state: 'server identifier' MUST NOT be filled in, 'requested IP address' option MUST NOT be filled in, 'ciaddr' MUST be filled in with client's IP address. This message MUST be broadcast to the 0xffffffff IP broadcast address.
statements.post_cond: message.server_identifier = null & message.requested_ip_address = null & message.ciaddr = client.ip_address & message.destination = 0xffffffff
actions: set ciaddr to client IP address

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST during SELECTING: Client inserts the address of the selected server in 'server identifier'.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST during SELECTING: 'ciaddr' MUST be zero.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST during SELECTING: 'requested IP address' MUST be filled in with the yiaddr value from the chosen DHCPOFFER.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST during INIT-REBOOT: 'server identifier' MUST NOT be filled in.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST during INIT-REBOOT: 'requested IP address' option MUST be filled in with client's notion of its previously assigned address.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST during INIT-REBOOT: 'ciaddr' MUST be zero.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST during RENEWING: 'server identifier' MUST NOT be filled in.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST during RENEWING: 'requested IP address' option MUST NOT be filled in.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST during RENEWING: 'ciaddr' MUST be filled in with client's IP address.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST during REBINDING: 'server identifier' MUST NOT be filled in.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST during REBINDING: 'requested IP address' option MUST NOT be filled in.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: DHCPREQUEST during REBINDING: 'ciaddr' MUST be filled in with client's IP address.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server receives a DHCPDECLINE message, the client has discovered through some other means that the suggested network address is already in use. The server MUST mark the network address as not available and SHOULD notify the local system administrator of a possible configuration problem.
actions: mark network address as not available
notify local system administrator of possible configuration problem

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server marks the network address as not allocated upon receipt of a DHCPRELEASE message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Upon receipt of a DHCPRELEASE message, the server marks the network address as not allocated. The server SHOULD retain a record of the client's initialization parameters for possible reuse in response to subsequent requests from the client.
actions: mark network address as not allocated
retain record of client's initialization parameters for possible reuse

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server responds to a DHCPINFORM message by sending a DHCPACK message directly to the address given in the 'ciaddr' field of the DHCPINFORM message.
actions: include parameters as defined in section 4.3.1

statements.subject: client
statements.description: INIT-REBOOT state: client sends broadcast DHCPREQUEST; server-ip MUST NOT be set; requested-ip MUST be set; ciaddr is zero

statements.subject: client
statements.description: SELECTING state: client sends broadcast DHCPREQUEST; server-ip MUST be set; requested-ip MUST be set; ciaddr is zero

statements.subject: client
statements.description: RENEWING state: client sends unicast DHCPREQUEST; server-ip MUST NOT be set; requested-ip MUST NOT be set; ciaddr is IP address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: REBINDING state: client sends broadcast DHCPREQUEST; server-ip MUST NOT be set; requested-ip MUST NOT be set; ciaddr is IP address

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In INIT-REBOOT state, client message MUST be broadcast

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In INIT-REBOOT state, server-ip MUST NOT be set in client message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In INIT-REBOOT state, requested-ip MUST be set in client message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In INIT-REBOOT state, ciaddr MUST be zero in client message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In SELECTING state, client message MUST be broadcast

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In SELECTING state, server-ip MUST be set in client message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In SELECTING state, requested-ip MUST be set in client message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In SELECTING state, ciaddr MUST be zero in client message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In RENEWING state, client message MUST be unicast

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In RENEWING state, server-ip MUST NOT be set in client message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In RENEWING state, requested-ip MUST NOT be set in client message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In RENEWING state, ciaddr MUST be set to the client's IP address in the client message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In REBINDING state, client message MUST be broadcast

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In REBINDING state, server-ip MUST NOT be set in client message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In REBINDING state, requested-ip MUST NOT be set in client message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In REBINDING state, ciaddr MUST be set to the client's IP address in the client message

statements.subject: client
statements.description: INIT-REBOOT state in the Figure 5 state-transition diagram for DHCP clients

statements.subject: client
statements.description: INIT state in the Figure 5 state-transition diagram for DHCP clients

statements.subject: client
statements.description: REBOOTING state in the Figure 5 state-transition diagram for DHCP clients

statements.subject: client
statements.description: SELECTING state in the Figure 5 state-transition diagram for DHCP clients

statements.subject: client
statements.description: REQUESTING state in the Figure 5 state-transition diagram for DHCP clients

statements.subject: client
statements.description: BOUND state in the Figure 5 state-transition diagram for DHCP clients

statements.description: RENEWING state in the Figure 5 state-transition diagram for DHCP clients

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From INIT-REBOOT, client sends DHCPREQUEST and transitions to REBOOTING (-/Send DHCPREQUEST)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REBOOTING, receipt of DHCPNAK causes restart; client transitions to INIT (DHCPNAK/Restart)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REBOOTING, receipt of DHCPACK causes client to record lease and set timers T1, T2, transitioning to BOUND (DHCPACK/Record lease, set timers T1, T2)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From INIT, client sends DHCPDISCOVER and transitions to SELECTING (-/Send DHCPDISCOVER)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In SELECTING, receipt of DHCPOFFER causes client to collect replies and remain in SELECTING (DHCPOFFER/Collect replies)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From SELECTING, client selects an offer and sends DHCPREQUEST, transitioning to REQUESTING (Select offer/send DHCPREQUEST)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In REQUESTING, receipt of DHCPOFFER is discarded; client remains in REQUESTING (DHCPOFFER/Discard)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REQUESTING, receipt of DHCPNAK causes client to discard offer and transition to INIT (DHCPNAK/Discard offer)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REQUESTING, if DHCPACK is not acceptable, client sends DHCPDECLINE and transitions to INIT (DHCPACK (not accept.)/Send DHCPDECLINE)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REQUESTING, receipt of acceptable DHCPACK causes client to record lease and set timers T1, T2, transitioning to BOUND (DHCPACK/Record lease, set timers T1, T2)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In BOUND, receipt of DHCPOFFER, DHCPACK, or DHCPNAK is discarded; client remains in BOUND (DHCPOFFER, DHCPACK, DHCPNAK/Discard)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From BOUND, when timer T1 expires, client sends DHCPREQUEST to leasing server and transitions to RENEWING (T1 expires/Send DHCPREQUEST to leasing server)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From RENEWING, receipt of DHCPACK causes client to record lease and set timers T1, T2, transitioning to BOUND (DHCPACK/Record lease, set timers T1, T2)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From RENEWING, when timer T2 expires, client broadcasts DHCPREQUEST and transitions to REBINDING (T2 expires/Broadcast DHCPREQUEST)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From RENEWING, receipt of DHCPNAK causes client to halt network and transition to INIT (DHCPNAK/Halt network)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REBINDING, receipt of DHCPACK causes client to record lease and set timers T1, T2, transitioning to BOUND (DHCPACK/Record lease, set timers T1,T2)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: From REBINDING, receipt of DHCPNAK or lease expiry causes client to halt network and transition to INIT (DHCPNAK, Lease expired/Halt network)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The DHCPINFORM message is not shown in figure 5. A client simply sends the DHCPINFORM and waits for DHCPACK messages. Once the client has selected its parameters, it has completed the configuration process.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client begins in INIT state and forms a DHCPDISCOVER message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once the DHCPACK message from the server arrives, the client is initialized and moves to BOUND state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: SELECTING state referenced in Table 5: 'Requested IP address MUST (in SELECTING or INIT-REBOOT)' and 'Server identifier MUST (after SELECTING)' in DHCPREQUEST.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: INIT-REBOOT state referenced in Table 5: 'Requested IP address MUST (in SELECTING or INIT-REBOOT)' and 'Server identifier MUST NOT (after INIT-REBOOT, BOUND, RENEWING or REBINDING)'.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: RENEWING state referenced in Table 5: 'Requested IP address MUST NOT (in BOUND or RENEWING)' and 'Server identifier MUST NOT (after INIT-REBOOT, BOUND, RENEWING or REBINDING)'.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: REBINDING state referenced in Table 5: 'ciaddr 0 or client's network address (BOUND/RENEW/REBIND)' and 'Server identifier MUST NOT (after INIT-REBOOT, BOUND, RENEWING or REBINDING)'.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client begins in INIT state and forms a DHCPDISCOVER message. The client generates and records a random transaction identifier and inserts that identifier into the 'xid' field. The client then broadcasts the DHCPDISCOVER on the local hardware broadcast address to the 0xffffffff IP broadcast address and 'DHCP server' UDP port.
statements.post_cond: client.xid_generated = true & client.local_time_recorded = true & client.dhcpdiscover_broadcast = true
actions: broadcast DHCPDISCOVER to 0xffffffff on DHCP server UDP port

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the parameters are acceptable, the client records the address of the server that supplied the parameters from the 'server identifier' field and sends that address in the 'server identifier' field of a DHCPREQUEST broadcast message.
statements.pre_cond: client.state = SELECTING & client.dhcpoffer_received = true & client.parameters_acceptable = true
actions: select one DHCPOFFER from collected offers
extract server identifier from DHCPOFFER server identifier option
broadcast DHCPREQUEST with server identifier and same xid as DHCPOFFER

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once the DHCPACK message from the server arrives, the client is initialized and moves to BOUND state. The client records the lease expiration time as the sum of the time at which the original request was sent and the duration of the lease from the DHCPACK message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the 'xid' of an arriving DHCPOFFER message does not match the 'xid' of the most recent DHCPDISCOVER message, the DHCPOFFER message must be silently discarded.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Any arriving DHCPACK messages must be silently discarded (during DHCPOFFER collection phase, before DHCPREQUEST is sent).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the network address appears to be in use, the client MUST send a DHCPDECLINE message to the server.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD broadcast an ARP reply to announce the client's new IP address and clear any outdated ARP cache entries in hosts on the client's subnet (after moving to BOUND state).
actions: broadcast ARP reply announcing new IP address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client begins in INIT-REBOOT state and sends a DHCPREQUEST message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a DHCPACK message with an 'xid' field matching that in the client's DHCPREQUEST message arrives from any server, the client is initialized and moves to BOUND state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client begins in INIT-REBOOT state and sends a DHCPREQUEST message broadcast on the local hardware broadcast address to the 'DHCP server' UDP port.
actions: insert known network address as 'requested IP address' option in DHCPREQUEST
generate and record random transaction identifier into 'xid' field
record local time for lease expiration computation
broadcast DHCPREQUEST to DHCP server UDP port on local hardware broadcast address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a DHCPACK message with an 'xid' field matching that in the client's DHCPREQUEST message arrives from any server, the client is initialized and moves to BOUND state.
statements.pre_cond: client.state = INIT-REBOOT & message.type = DHCPACK & message.xid = client.xid
actions: record lease expiration time as sum of DHCPREQUEST send time and lease duration from DHCPACK

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The client MUST insert its known network address as a 'requested IP address' option in the DHCPREQUEST message.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The client MUST NOT include a 'server identifier' in the DHCPREQUEST message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a DHCPACK message with an 'xid' field matching that in the client's DHCPINFORM message arrives from any server, the client is initialized.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client sends a DHCPINFORM message. The client generates and records a random transaction identifier and inserts that identifier into the 'xid' field. The client places its own network address in the 'ciaddr' field.
statements.trigger: initialization with externally assigned network address
actions: generate and record random transaction identifier
insert transaction identifier into xid field
place own network address in ciaddr field
unicast DHCPINFORM to server if server address known, else broadcast to limited broadcast address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a DHCPACK message with an 'xid' field matching that in the client's DHCPINFORM message arrives from any server, the client is initialized.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client does not receive a DHCPACK within a reasonable period of time (60 seconds or 4 tries if using timeout suggested in section 4.1), then it SHOULD display a message informing the user of the problem, and then SHOULD begin network processing using suitable defaults as per Appendix A.
actions: display message informing user of the problem
begin network processing using suitable defaults

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Once a DHCPACK message with an 'xid' field matching that in the client's DHCPINFORM message arrives from any server, the client is initialized.

statements.description: When the DHCP client knows the address of a DHCP server, in either INIT or REBOOTING state, the client may use that address in the DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST rather than the IP broadcast address.

statements.description: When the DHCP client knows the address of a DHCP server, in either INIT or REBOOTING state, the client may use that address in the DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST rather than the IP broadcast address.

statements.subject: client

actions: unicast DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST to known server address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the DHCP client knows the address of a DHCP server, in either INIT or REBOOTING state, the client may use that address in the DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST rather than the IP broadcast address.
actions: unicast DHCPREQUEST to known server address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client receives no response to DHCP messages sent to the IP address of a known DHCP server, the DHCP client reverts to using the IP broadcast address.
actions: revert to sending DHCP messages to IP broadcast address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client unicasts DHCPRELEASE messages to the server. Because the client is declining the use of the IP address supplied by the server, the client broadcasts DHCPDECLINE messages.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Because the client is declining the use of the IP address supplied by the server, the client broadcasts DHCPDECLINE messages.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: T1 is the time at which the client enters the RENEWING state and attempts to contact the server that originally issued the client's network address.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: T2 is the time at which the client enters the REBINDING state and attempts to contact any server.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client has successfully reacquired its network address, returns to BOUND state and may continue network processing.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the lease expires before the client receives a DHCPACK, the client moves to INIT state, MUST immediately stop any other network processing and requests network initialization parameters as if the client were uninitialized.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: At time T1 the client moves to RENEWING state and sends (via unicast) a DHCPREQUEST message to the server to extend its lease.
actions: set ciaddr to current network address
record local time of DHCPREQUEST transmission

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the client receives a DHCPACK from the server, the client computes the lease expiration time as the sum of the time at which the client sent the DHCPREQUEST message and the duration of the lease in the DHCPACK message. The client has successfully reacquired its network address, returns to BOUND state and may continue network processing.
actions: compute lease expiration time as DHCPREQUEST_send_time + lease_duration

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If no DHCPACK arrives before time T2, the client moves to REBINDING state and sends (via broadcast) a DHCPREQUEST message to extend its lease.
statements.pre_cond: client.state = RENEWING & timer.T2 = expired & DHCPACK.received = false
actions: set ciaddr to current network address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the lease expires before the client receives a DHCPACK, the client moves to INIT state, MUST immediately stop any other network processing and requests network initialization parameters as if the client were uninitialized.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In both RENEWING and REBINDING states, if the client receives no response to its DHCPREQUEST message, the client SHOULD wait one-half of the remaining time until T2 (in RENEWING state), down to a minimum of 60 seconds, before retransmitting the DHCPREQUEST message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In both RENEWING and REBINDING states, if the client receives no response to its DHCPREQUEST message, the client SHOULD wait one-half of the remaining lease time (in REBINDING state), down to a minimum of 60 seconds, before retransmitting the DHCPREQUEST message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client MAY choose to renew or extend its lease prior to T1.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The client MUST NOT include a 'server identifier' in the DHCPREQUEST message (in RENEWING and REBINDING states).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client no longer requires use of its assigned network address (e.g., the client is gracefully shut down), the client sends a DHCPRELEASE message to the server.
